sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the June 1930 Gloucester City series, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and showing the western half of the Borough of Brooklawn, the planned garden suburb laid out during the First World War for shipyard workers. The built-up part lies in the upper half of the sheet, between the marsh along Little Timber Creek and Chestnut Street, and is laid out on a radial and curving plan: Pershing Road loops around the west end, Paris Avenue and New Jersey Road cross on diagonals, and Pennsylvania Road and Marne Road run towards Chestnut Street. Small two-storey frame dwellings, many in semi-detached pairs and short rows, stand on narrow lots, with a few concrete-block garages. Between Chestnut Street and New Broadway two long blocks are divided by internal footways around small open courts. A sewage disposal plant with a concrete tank and pump house sits on the marsh edge north of New Jersey Road, and a water works pumping station stands in the oval of Town Center. The lower half of the sheet is planned but empty: Center, Town Center, Pennsylvania Road, Marne Road, New Jersey Road, Chestnut and a proposed street are drawn as unopened streets around large numbered blocks, with a traffic circle at the south-east corner on New Broadway. Big Timber Creek and Little Timber Creek with an island and marsh fill the west and north, crossed by a wooden foot bridge at the end of Pershing Road. Broadway appears at the top right edge beside the sheet 20 boundary.
notes: Streets in the lower half of the sheet are marked not open; modern streets there follow another plan (Timber Boulevard near the old Center), so the south half has no control points and is placed by extrapolation.
New Broadway is now US 130 and has been widened; it was left out of the control (including it raised RMSE from 1.1 to 2.4 m).
Chestnut is lettered without a suffix; today it is Chestnut Street.
The street lettered Broadway at the top right is Old Broadway today.

Map, 100 ft. Printed sheet 21 of the Gloucester City series: western Brooklawn (Pershing Rd, New Jersey Rd, Paris Av, Pennsylvania Rd, Marne Rd, Chestnut, Town Center); south half planned streets marked not open, Big and Little Timber Creek to the west. One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 of the June 1930 Gloucester City series, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and showing the eastern half of the Borough of Brooklawn. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs down the left side beside Railroad Avenue and Broadway, with New Broadway and a row of houses, stores and a bakery along its west side; Marne Road, New Jersey Road and Town Center come in from sheet 21. North of Browning Lane a grid of 2nd to 7th Streets and Center is laid out in long lots, mostly vacant, with the Borough Hall, the American Marine and Aviation Glue Company, several stores and garages near the railroad. South of Browning Lane the planned village spreads around Noreg Place, a circle from which Bergen, Haakon Road, Nansen Avenue, Maude Avenue and footways radiate, with Christiana, Delaware Avenue, South Hannevig Avenue, Wilson Avenue and Horten Avenue around it. Houses are small frame dwellings, many in pairs and short rows. Institutions include the Brooklawn Public School, the M.E. Church and the Brooklawn Volunteer Fire Company, and a fire alarm siren stands on a steel tower in a small oval at Broadway and Wilson Avenue, with a pedestrian tunnel under the tracks. Kings Highway (Mount Ephraim Road) crosses the lower right towards Crescent Boulevard and Crescent Plaza, and a dash-dot line marks the boundary between the Boroughs of Brooklawn and Bellmawr. Two traffic circles appear along the bottom edge; much of the lower right is open land.
notes: Renamed since: Broadway is Old Broadway, Horten Avenue is Horton Avenue, Bergen is Bergen Street, Christiana is Christiana Street, Delaware Avenue is Delaware Street, South Hannevig Avenue north of Broadway is North Hannevig Avenue.
Kings Highway (Mount Ephraim Road) is now Crescent Boulevard (US 130) through Brooklawn; widened, so left out of the control.
New Broadway (US 130) left out of the control because it has been widened.
Lake Drive was not used for control: its modern junctions with the numbered streets lie at or beyond the top edge of the sheet.
The railroad is lettered W.J. and S. R.R. (P.R.R.).
Sheet 22 fits at 3.98 px/ft against 3.95 for sheet 21 (about 1 percent).
Map, 100 ft. Printed sheet 22: eastern Brooklawn (Broadway, Railroad Av, 2nd-7th Sts, Browning Lane, Noreg Pl circle, Haakon Rd, Bergen, Hannevig, Horten Av, Kings Hwy). One part.
